title: Apple releases iOS 27, macOS Golden Gate 27 with Siri AI and Liquid Glass refinements
gist: Apple shipped its 2026 OS wave (iOS 27, macOS 27 Golden Gate, watchOS/visionOS/tvOS 27) with an LLM-based Siri overhaul as the flagship feature, powered by in-house AFM 3 models split across a 3B on-device core, a 20B sparse on-device model activating 1-4B parameters per request, and several cloud models. Siri AI is gated to iPhone 15 Pro / iPhone 16 and later, and Golden Gate is the final macOS release to support Rosetta Intel translation.

insights.claim: Apple Intelligence features are driven primarily by Apple's own models labeled AFM 3 rather than by a third-party frontier lab's model, spanning on-device and cloud tiers.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple is keeping the model layer in-house, capping the revenue that external LLM vendors can extract from the ~2bn-device installed base; watch for any Apple disclosure of paid external inference.
insights.quote: Siri AI and other “Apple Intelligence” features are primarily driven by a handful of Apple-developed models, most of them labeled AFM 3.
insights.locator: Siri AI and other “Apple Intelligence” features are primarily driven...

insights.claim: Apple's on-device stack now has two tiers: AFM 3 Core at 3 billion parameters, and AFM 3 Core Advanced at 20 billion parameters using a sparse architecture that activates only 1 to 4 billion parameters per request.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Sparse activation lets Apple run a 20B-class model inside a phone's memory and thermal budget, pushing more inference off cloud GPUs and onto silicon Apple already sells.
insights.quote: uses a sparse architecture, activating just 1 to 4 billion parameters at a time depending on the request
insights.locator: On-device, there’s AFM 3 Core with 3 billion parameters

insights.claim: Apple maintains a three-model cloud tier alongside on-device models: AFM 3 Cloud, ADM 3 Cloud (Image), and AFM3 Cloud Pro, indicating heavier requests still route to Apple-operated remote servers.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A named cloud tier implies continued Apple datacenter/server-silicon capex rather than a purely on-device strategy.
insights.locator: On top of that, there are AFM 3 Cloud, ADM 3 Cloud (Image), and AFM3 Cloud Pro

insights.claim: The split between a 3B always-available core model and a 20B sparse model implies Apple is tiering assistant quality by device memory rather than by subscription, making silicon generation the gate on AI capability.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Device-gated AI is an upgrade-cycle lever: it converts model improvements into hardware replacement demand instead of recurring software revenue.
insights.locator: On-device, there’s AFM 3 Core with 3 billion parameters

themes.theme: LLM Siri as an app-layer platform

insights.claim: Apple's rebuilt Siri can explain what is on screen and search a user's personal history including old emails and text messages, making private on-device data the assistant's differentiating context source.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Personal-context retrieval is a moat cloud chatbots cannot replicate without the same OS-level data access; it pressures standalone assistant apps.
insights.locator: The new Siri can respond in kind to natural language requests

insights.claim: Siri can now directly operate third-party applications, but only where developers have explicitly added support for that integration.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Assistant usefulness is gated on developer adoption, so the metric to track is how many top-grossing apps ship Siri action support, not the model benchmark.
insights.quote: It can also directly interact with applications when developers have added support for that.
insights.locator: It can also directly interact with applications

insights.claim: Apple has shipped a dedicated Siri app resembling the standalone ChatGPT and Claude apps, moving the assistant from an invisible system layer to a competing destination app.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A preinstalled chat destination on every iPhone is direct distribution competition for OpenAI and Anthropic consumer apps.
insights.quote: There’s now a dedicated Siri app, kind of similar in some respects to the classic ChatGPT or Claude apps.
insights.locator: There’s now a dedicated Siri app

insights.claim: Apple's new AI features include generating Shortcut automations and Safari browser extensions from a natural-language prompt, pushing code-generation capability into mainstream consumer software.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Prompt-to-extension lowers the floor for simple utility apps and erodes the market for cheap single-purpose automation software.
insights.locator: Other new AI features include the ability to generate Shortcut automations

themes.theme: Hardware gating and the upgrade cycle

insights.claim: iOS 27 installs on iPhone 11 and later, but Siri AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or an iPhone 16 or newer, so a large share of the supported installed base gets the OS without the flagship feature.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The four-generation gap between OS support and AI support is the clearest quantified driver of an Apple replacement supercycle.
insights.quote: iOS 27 supports the iPhone 11 and later, but you’ll need either an iPhone 15 Pro or an iPhone 16 or later to use Siri AI.

insights.claim: macOS 27 Golden Gate requires an M-series Mac, formally ending new-OS support for Intel-based Macs.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A hard silicon cutoff forces remaining Intel Mac holders into a purchase decision this cycle.
insights.quote: Golden Gate requires an M-series Mac.

insights.claim: tvOS 27 ships entirely without the new Siri AI features, showing Apple is allocating its AI effort only to devices with the silicon and the personal-data context to justify it.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple's AI rollout is device-economics driven, so expect low-margin/low-memory product lines to lag indefinitely.
insights.locator: tvOS completely lacks the new Siri AI features

themes.theme: Rosetta sunset and legacy software breakage

insights.claim: macOS Golden Gate is the final macOS version to support Rosetta, the translation layer that lets Apple Silicon Macs run older Intel-based applications.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: A dated end-of-life for Intel app compatibility creates a forced-migration deadline for enterprise and pro software vendors still shipping x86 binaries.
insights.quote: Golden Gate is the last version of macOS to support Rosetta
insights.locator: It’s also worth noting that Golden Gate is the last version

insights.claim: After this macOS cycle many older unmaintained applications will simply stop working, though Apple carved out a specific exception preserving older games built for Intel Macs.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: The gaming carve-out signals Apple treats catalog depth as strategically valuable while treating legacy productivity software as expendable.
insights.quote: After this cycle, many older unmaintained apps will stop working, but Apple did carve out an exception for older games that were developed for Intel Macs.
insights.locator: After this cycle, many older unmaintained apps will stop working

themes.theme: Liquid Glass retreat and quality-of-life polish

insights.claim: Apple added a user-facing slider controlling how transparent or opaque the Liquid Glass design appears across iOS and macOS, effectively making its signature redesign optional.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Shipping an opt-out for a flagship design language is an admission the redesign was poorly received; a reminder Apple now responds to backlash faster than historically.
insights.quote: users now have a slider to affect how transparent or opaque the “Liquid Glass” design is across the operating system

insights.claim: This macOS release contains no radically new design ideas and is instead a polish pass responding to user feedback accumulated since Liquid Glass launched.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple is spending a full annual cycle repairing rather than extending the UI, which suggests engineering attention has shifted to the AI stack.
insights.quote: There’s nothing radically new in terms of design here, but this is a much-needed polish pass.
insights.locator: And on the macOS side especially, Apple has made numerous small design tweaks

insights.claim: macOS now supports HDR across all system UI elements and adds more robust support for a wider range of external monitor display modes.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: System-wide HDR and broader external-display support are small tailwinds for premium monitor demand among Mac professionals.
insights.locator: For example, macOS now supports HDR for all system UI elements

insights.claim: watchOS 27 adds perimenopause and menopause notifications and tracking alongside more accurate step counting, while removing little-used features such as Walkie Talkie.
insights.speaker: Samuel Axon
insights.so_what: Apple keeps extending Apple Watch into clinically adjacent women's health tracking, a category where it is building a data moat against Fitbit-class rivals.
insights.locator: watchOS adds the Siri app and Siri AI, a new watch face
